title: Make all GDELT ingest timestamps explicitly UTC-aware
context: A live local dry run against a real (non-UTC) ClickHouse Cloud instance proved a timezone bug: main.py builds every GDELT-derived timestamp as a naive datetime (datetime.strptime with no tzinfo), correctly intending it to represent UTC (GDELT publishes 14-digit timestamps in UTC). But clickhouse_connect interprets a naive Python datetime using the local system timezone when serializing it for a ClickHouse DateTime column, then converts to UTC for storage. On this machine (EDT, UTC-4), a written gdelt.ingest_log.file_timestamp came back as 23:15 when main.py computed 19:15 -- exactly a +4h shift. Because fetch_lastupdate()'s `latest` is pure string parsing with no ClickHouse round-trip, it stays correct while values read back from ClickHouse are corrupted -- that asymmetry broke _candidates_to_process's gap detection outright (earliest ended up after latest, so candidate_timestamps produced nothing). The same corruption path affects gdelt.events.DATEADDED, gdelt.mentions.EventTimeDate/MentionTimeDate, and the idempotency delete's {ts:DateTime} parameter in delete_existing_rows. The fully-mocked test suite (tests/test_main.py, StubClickHouseClient) never catches this since its stub never actually serializes a datetime through clickhouse_connect.
verification: pip install -q -r requirements.txt && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
constraints: No change to the idempotency delete-then-insert ordering, the gap-detection algorithm's semantics, or the masterfilelist fallback logic -- only the timezone representation of the datetimes involved
No changes to bootstrap.sql, alters.sql, or any ClickHouse schema -- this is a main.py-only bug fix

tasks.title: Make every GDELT timestamp UTC-aware end to end, plus a UTC session timezone as defense in depth
tasks.why: A live run against real ClickHouse (non-UTC host) proved every stored/compared GDELT timestamp silently drifts by the local UTC offset, corrupting ingest_log gap-detection and the events/mentions DATEADDED-family columns.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every datetime main.py constructs to represent a real GDELT moment in time -- _to_datetime's return value, fetch_lastupdate's parsed `latest`, and any timestamp passed to delete_existing_rows/process_timestamp/_write_ingest_log -- is timezone-aware with tzinfo=timezone.utc, never naive.

_ingest_log_state's timestamps read back from gdelt.ingest_log (via the ClickHouse client) are normalized to UTC-aware before being compared against a freshly-parsed `latest`, so candidate_timestamps/_candidates_to_process never raises 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes' and never silently misbehaves from a naive/aware mismatch.

get_client() explicitly configures a UTC session/client timezone on the clickhouse_connect client (defense in depth), so datetime serialization cannot fall back to interpreting a naive value using the local system timezone.
_to_date continues to return a plain date (dates carry no tzinfo) and is unaffected/uncorrupted by this change -- no regression on the 'Day' field.

tests/test_main.py's fixtures/helpers (_ts(), StubClickHouseClient, row builders) are updated to construct and assert UTC-aware datetimes consistently, and at least one new test explicitly asserts _to_datetime, fetch_lastupdate, and candidate_timestamps all produce UTC-aware (not naive) datetimes.
The full existing test suite still passes, with no test weakened, skipped, or removed to get there.
